lines: I heard your apology. What you do next will tell me more.
I will not erase what happened, but I can add what happens after.
Those words are a start. They are not the repair.
I accept that you regret it. I need to see that you understand it.
Do not make me hear the same apology for the same harm twice.
The record can change without pretending the first entry vanished.
You spoke plainly. I appreciate that much.
I am willing to continue, carefully.
An apology matters most when it costs you the old behavior.
I believe you are sorry. Trust may take longer.
Thank you for naming what you did instead of hiding behind intent.
I can forgive without becoming careless.
We do not need a grand speech. We need a better pattern.
I will give you room to prove those words true.
That explains your choice. It does not excuse the damage.
I am still angry, but I am listening.
Let us call this the beginning of the correction.
I accept the apology. Please do not ask me to forget.
If you mean it, the difference will become visible soon enough.
All right. We move forward, one careful step at a time.
